dedupe_keys.name: water systems integrated modelling framework wsimod

description: WSIMOD provides a Python framework for integrating water quantity and quality processes across a water system. Imperial College London contributors developed it to represent connections that isolated subsystem models can miss. The repository includes representations of rivers, reservoirs, treatment plants, pipe networks and urban or rural hydrological catchments. Components communicate water flux and quality information through a message-passing interface, with nodes and arcs defining a model. Geographic coverage, forcing period and temporal resolution depend on the user-defined application; the package is not a fixed catchment dataset. GitHub publishes the source, tutorials and installation instructions under BSD-3-Clause, allowing free reuse. Limitations include the need to configure connected components and supply appropriate local inputs; this review did not reproduce a calibrated simulation. Uses include water-management scenarios and examination of interactions across supply, wastewater and catchment processes. Related records model-epanet and model-wntr cover distribution-network modelling, whereas WSIMOD connects a wider water cycle. Its README cites both a JOSS software paper and a GMD methods paper. The old repository address redirects to ImperialCollegeLondon/wsi.
